ch14.d.ratio: Throat area $A_2$ over the wide area $A_1$; 1 means a uniform pipe
ch14.d.Q: Volume of water crossing any cross-section per second
ch14.d.dy: Height of the outlet above the inlet; the pipe tilts by that much
ch14.goal.cont: Continuity: the flow rate $Q = Av$ is the same everywhere in the pipe, so the water is faster where the pipe is narrow
ch14.goal.bern: Bernoulli: $p + \tfrac{1}{2}\rho v^2 + \rho g y$ is constant, so the pressure is lower where the water is faster
ch14.obs.tracer: Tracers enter at equal time intervals; in the throat their spacing grows by $A_1/A_2$
ch14.obs.column: Standpipe column height $= p/\rho g$; the level is lowest at the throat (2)
ch14.obs.table: Table: the $Av$ row and the sum row are equal at all three taps; $p$ and $\tfrac{1}{2}\rho v^2$ trade off
ch14.obs.ratio: Area ratio 1: speed and pressure stay constant. Ratio 0.5: $v_2 = 2v_1$ and $p_1 - p_2 = \tfrac{1}{2}\rho (v_2^2 - v_1^2)$
ch14.obs.tilt: Height difference 20 cm: taps 1 and 3 have the same speed, but the pressure at the higher outlet (3) is lower by $\rho g \Delta y$
ch14.assume.flow: Incompressible, steady, non-viscous flow (water, $\rho = 1000\ \text{kg/m}^3$), uniform speed across each cross-section
ch14.assume.p: $p$ is gauge pressure (relative to the atmosphere); height $y$ is measured from the inlet axis. The inlet pressure is chosen so that every column stands above the pipe
